title: Auto Loans: Linking a Late Charge to Its Autopay Debit
content:
To judge whether an Auto Loans late charge stems from PCB's handling of an autopay debit, the late charge has to be tied to the debit for its installment. This note fixes how that link is made.

## Rule

- **The late charge examined** is the one most recently posted to the loan, together with the installment date it carries.
- **The debit** is the latest autopay payment from a PCB checking account that was applied toward that same installment date.
- **Returned or not:** the debit counts as returned when a payment reversal on the loan's activity names it as its related entry; when no reversal names it, it does not count as returned.

All three are read from the loan's activity.

## From the records to the link

| Input | Judgement | Output |
|---|---|---|
| the loan's late charges | pick the one posted most recently | the late charge and its installment date |
| autopay payments applied toward that installment date | pick the latest | the debit |
| payment reversal entries | is there one naming the debit | returned, or not returned |

## Illustration (hypothetical activity)

The newest late charge on a loan was posted on 26 June for the installment dated 10 June. Two autopay payments were applied toward the 10 June installment, on 10 June and on 12 June; the one of 12 June is the debit. A reversal names the 12 June payment, so the debit counts as returned.
